name: ARMADA Marine Robotics
institution_or_company: Spinout of Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI)
researcher_or_founder: Robin Littlefield (co-founder, WHOI engineer); Jeff Kaeli (co-founder, WHOI engineer)
technology: Asymmetric Propulsion: varies the speed of a single-bladed propeller through each rotation to deliver both thrust and steering from one motor, removing fins and secondary motors from underwater vehicles
current_maturity: Company formed; IP licensed; STTR Phase I underway
evidence_signal: Two granted US patents (Asymmetric Propulsion US 9,873,499; Rotational Feedback Control US 11,990,857); technology developed and tested at WHOI over years
commercialization_signal: Two exclusive WHOI license agreements executed Jan 2025; NSF STTR Phase I contract of $255,821 to develop Asymmetric Propulsion with WHOI
why_potentially_interesting: Textbook research-to-venture transition at Propeller's own founding partner institution: WHOI IP, WHOI engineer founders, formal exclusive license, then competitive federal commercialization funding. Attacks vehicle cost at the actuator level rather than building another vehicle.
biggest_unknown: Whether removing actuators preserves enough control authority in real currents and sea states - and whether vehicle cost is actually the customer's binding constraint versus launch, recovery and support-ship cost
propeller_relevance: Category 1 (Industrials); WHOI is Propeller's founding partner; dual-use, which Propeller has written about explicitly; pre-seed stage fits the stated $500K-$3M model

name: Juice Robotics
institution_or_company: Spinout of University of Rhode Island
researcher_or_founder: Matthew Jewell (CTO, URI alumnus); Brennan Phillips (CSO, URI Professor); Stephen Piper (CEO, former IBM executive)
technology: Miniaturised underwater sensing, communications and robotics. Named technology 'High Dive' is a platform linking aerial and underwater systems via an ultra-light fibre-optic tether for real-time comms, sensing and control
current_maturity: Company formed; four university technologies licensed; first institutional investment raised
evidence_signal: Four URI technologies licensed; two years operating inside URI's Ocean Technology Center incubator; founding team includes the URI professor who created the technology
commercialization_signal: Licensed four URI technologies and secured investment from Rogue Island Ventures, announced 1 Jul 2026
why_potentially_interesting: Very recent (seven weeks before this research) multi-patent license plus first institutional round out of a Propeller partner institution. Air-to-water tethering sidesteps the underwater bandwidth bottleneck rather than trying to beat it.
biggest_unknown: Only one of the four licensed technologies (High Dive) is publicly named; the other three are undisclosed, so the actual IP position cannot be assessed from public sources. Round size also undisclosed.
propeller_relevance: Category 1 (Industrials); URI is a Propeller partner; explicitly commercial, scientific and defence applications, matching Propeller's dual-use thesis; seed stage

name: Sea-Gal Technologies, Inc.
technology: High-frequency MIMO underwater acoustic communications, deliberately operating outside the frequency range of marine mammal communication to reduce ecosystem impact
current_maturity: Company formed; SBIR Phase I awarded
evidence_signal: NSF SBIR Phase I award 2451589 ($304,999), competitively awarded on technical and commercial merit
why_potentially_interesting: Underwater communications bandwidth is a first-order constraint on every autonomy, sensing and mCDR-MRV application in this taxonomy - it is an enabling layer, not an application. Underwater acoustic communications is not represented in the publicly disclosed Propeller portfolio reviewed.
biggest_unknown: Whether MIMO gains hold in real multipath-limited shallow-water channels, and whether the buyer is a component OEM or an end user - which determines whether this is a chip/module business or a systems business
propeller_relevance: Category 2 (Industrials/Carbon enabling); horizontal enabler beneath several Propeller portfolio companies; pre-seed/seed

name: atdepth MRV
technology: GPU-based real-time ocean modelling system enabling multi-scale simulation from global ocean down to metre scale, combined with in-water monitoring, for MRV of marine carbon dioxide removal
current_maturity: Company formed; major federal program award; commercial partnership announced
evidence_signal: ARPA-E SEA-CO2 award of $2,524,964 for a scalable, integrated, real-time GPU-based modelling system for mCDR MRV
commercialization_signal: ARPA-E SEA-CO2 program award; partnership with Deep Sky to advance direct ocean capture in Canada; SeaAhead/BlueSwell alumnus
why_potentially_interesting: MRV is the gating problem for the entire mCDR sector and is where the science is genuinely unsettled - a picks-and-shovels position beneath the crowded capture market rather than another capture technology
biggest_unknown: Whether MRV is a durable standalone business or gets absorbed into registries, capture developers, or public models; and whether GPU speed is a defensible advantage rather than a temporary engineering lead
propeller_relevance: Category 4 (Carbon) - Propeller's densest theme, with Aquatic Labs as the closest disclosed adjacency; complementary rather than competitive with capture companies

name: Hydrokinetx Corporation
technology: Wave-energy harvesting to provide persistent power for ocean sensing platforms, replacing batteries and solar which fail in remote or cloudy conditions
current_maturity: Company formed; STTR Phase I awarded
evidence_signal: NSF STTR Phase I award 2537673 ($304,950); STTR structure implies a university research partner
why_potentially_interesting: Targets the power bottleneck that limits every persistent ocean sensing deployment. Framed as an enabler of ocean data rather than as grid-scale marine energy, which avoids the capital intensity that has historically killed wave energy companies
biggest_unknown: Whether a wave energy converter small enough to power a sensor can be made cheaper and more reliable than simply oversizing batteries or using a larger solar array - the honest competitive benchmark
propeller_relevance: Category 2/3 (Industrials); directly enables the ocean-data thesis Propeller articulates around Aquatic Labs; pre-seed

name: Designer Ecosystems LLC
technology: Engineered submerged barrier structures combining coastal protection with ecological restoration, plus a sensor platform to measure real-world performance
current_maturity: Company formed; progressed SBIR Phase I to Phase II
evidence_signal: NSF SBIR Phase I 2436946 ($301,769, Apr 2025) followed by SBIR Phase II 2604863 ($1,242,694, Jul 2026) - Phase II requires demonstrated Phase I technical milestones
commercialization_signal: Two sequential NSF SBIR awards; Phase II awarded 24 Jul 2026
why_potentially_interesting: One of very few candidates with a full Phase I to Phase II progression, and the pairing of structure with a sensor platform means performance is measured rather than asserted - unusual in nature-based coastal protection
biggest_unknown: Who actually pays. Coastal protection buyers are frequently municipalities on grant cycles; the venture case depends on reaching insurers, developers or industrial asset owners
propeller_relevance: Category 6 (Industrials/adaptation); matches Propeller's Aug 2026 coastal adaptation thesis and the disclosed stealth company in coastal adaptation

name: Lightthought LLC
technology: Image-based AI system for high-resolution, low-latency imaging in turbid submerged environments for aquaculture monitoring
current_maturity: Company formed; STTR Phase I awarded
evidence_signal: NSF STTR Phase I award 2605022 ($304,925), implying a university research partner
commercialization_signal: NSF STTR Phase I, 18 Aug 2026 - three days before this research
why_potentially_interesting: Underwater machine vision in turbid water is a hard, unsolved sensing problem; aquaculture is Propeller's thinnest named theme with only one disclosed company
biggest_unknown: Whether aquaculture producers will pay for monitoring hardware given thin margins, and whether the imaging advantage is optics, algorithms, or both
propeller_relevance: Category 7 (Organics); Propeller's least-represented named theme; pre-seed

name: Cultimar Technologies, Inc.
technology: Chemical protein filtration method to remove off-flavour compounds from aquaculture production
current_maturity: Company formed; SBIR Phase I awarded
evidence_signal: NSF SBIR Phase I award 2537706 ($304,645)
why_potentially_interesting: Attacks a specific, quantified producer pain point rather than a general platform. The award abstract states off-flavour adds $4.5B in production costs and reduces farmer profitability by 20-30% (claim attributed to the abstract, not independently verified)
biggest_unknown: Whether the filtration method works across species and system types, and whether producers pay per-unit or per-installation - which changes the business model entirely
propeller_relevance: Category 7 (Organics); underrepresented theme; Puerto Rico base is outside the usual US ocean-tech geography

name: Nexuma L.L.C.
technology: Microbially-driven reinforcement of porous limestone to form an underground barrier against bottom-up flooding, saltwater intrusion and seawall failure
current_maturity: Company formed; SBIR Phase II awarded
evidence_signal: NSF SBIR Phase II award 2604891 ($1,149,796) - Phase II implies Phase I technical milestones met
why_potentially_interesting: Addresses bottom-up flooding through porous limestone, a failure mode conventional seawalls do not solve, in the single most exposed US coastal market (South Florida)
biggest_unknown: Durability and permanence of microbially-induced mineralisation under continuous saltwater flux, and whether permitting treats it as a structure or a subsurface injection
propeller_relevance: Category 6 (Industrials/adaptation); matches Propeller's stated adaptation interest

name: Grow Oyster Reefs, LLC
technology: Biomimetic 3D-printed metal moulds to mass-produce modular biophilic concrete reef substrate that replicates natural oyster settlement surfaces
current_maturity: Company formed; SBIR Phase II awarded
evidence_signal: NSF SBIR Phase II award 2528142 ($1,237,446)
why_potentially_interesting: The innovation is the manufacturing method rather than the structure - moulds for mass production, which is what converts a restoration project into a product business. Abstract cites 85% of US coastal oyster habitat degraded or lost
biggest_unknown: Whether buyers are restoration grant programmes (project revenue) or coastal developers and infrastructure owners (product revenue) - determines venture viability
propeller_relevance: Category 5 (Industrials/materials); marine concrete adjacency to Allium Engineering

name: Hybrid Reefs
institution_or_company: Spinout of Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego
researcher_or_founder: Daniel Wangpraseurt (founder; Associate Research Scientist, Coral Reef Engineering Lab); Alex Ferre; Mike Poirier; Samapti Kundu (CTO)
technology: Patent-pending nature-inspired biomaterials for coral restoration: CoralGuard (antifouling coating suppressing algal overgrowth), Snap-X (larval settlement attractant), Symbion (bleaching mitigation under heat stress)
current_maturity: Spinout formed; patent-pending platform; accelerator graduate
evidence_signal: Patent-pending biomaterials platform developed in a named Scripps lab; 2026 UC San Diego Chancellor's Innovation Awards Startup of the Year finalist
commercialization_signal: StartBlue Ocean Enterprise Accelerator (Cohort 1); featured at the UN Ocean Conference
why_potentially_interesting: The antifouling coating (CoralGuard) may be the more commercially interesting asset than the reef restoration application itself - marine antifouling is a large regulated market under pressure to move off biocides, and Propeller has written about hull coatings
biggest_unknown: Whether the business is reef restoration (grant-funded, hard venture market) or marine biomaterials (large commercial market). These imply completely different companies
propeller_relevance: Category 5; Scripps is a Propeller partner; antifouling chemistry is not represented in the publicly disclosed portfolio reviewed

name: Ocean Motion Technologies
researcher_or_founder: Dr. Jack Pan (founder, oceanographer and data scientist)
technology: Small-scale wave energy converters designed to power persistent at-sea data collection - framed by the company as enabling an 'Ocean of Things'
current_maturity: Company formed 2018; WEC work began 2020; DOE-supported
evidence_signal: DOE water power programme engagement documented by the Department of Energy; StartBlue Cohort 4 participant
commercialization_signal: DOE resources; StartBlue accelerator; named target markets include ocean observation, offshore aquaculture, coastal security and defence
why_potentially_interesting: Same persistent-power thesis as Hydrokinetx but further along, and a useful comparator for judging whether small-scale WEC economics actually close
biggest_unknown: Founded 2018 - by 2026 the absence of a disclosed large financing or named commercial customer is itself a question about traction or capital efficiency
propeller_relevance: Category 2/3 (Industrials); enables the ocean data thesis; stage fit needs verification given company age

name: AI-Enabled Autonomous Subsea Connection System
technology: Autonomous system that connects and disconnects underwater equipment without divers, handling the control problem created by constant wave motion
current_maturity: Pre-company; NSF I-Corps customer discovery underway
evidence_signal: NSF I-Corps award 2630206-series ($50,000); Hollinger leads an established robotics research group at OSU
commercialization_signal: NSF I-Corps, 17 Aug 2026 - four days before this research; I-Corps requires structured customer discovery
why_potentially_interesting: Subsea connection is named by Propeller itself as a hard problem in its ocean-compute post. Commercial diving is described in the award abstract as one of the world's most dangerous professions, so there is a safety driver alongside cost. OSU is a Propeller partner but this sits in the engineering college, not the oceanography college
biggest_unknown: Whether a startup can displace incumbent wet-mate connector suppliers, and whether autonomous connection is a product or a feature of existing ROV service providers
propeller_relevance: Category 1/3 (Industrials); OSU is a Propeller partner; directly relevant to offshore wind, subsea cable and ocean-compute interconnect

name: Marine-adapted RFID and analytics for shellfish aquaculture
institution_or_company: Virginia Institute of Marine Science, College of William & Mary
technology: Marine-adapted RFID tagging plus analytics for digital inventory management on commercial shellfish farms, replacing handwritten logs and spreadsheets
current_maturity: Pre-company; NSF I-Corps customer discovery underway
evidence_signal: NSF I-Corps award 2637876 ($50,000); VIMS is a leading shellfish aquaculture research institution and Walton is an established shellfish aquaculture researcher
commercialization_signal: NSF I-Corps, 19 Aug 2026 - two days before this research
why_potentially_interesting: Unusually concrete problem statement: farms managing millions of animals on handwritten logs. Grounded in a real operational pain rather than a technology looking for a use
biggest_unknown: Whether shellfish growers, who are typically small and capital-constrained, will pay for tagging hardware plus software - the classic willingness-to-pay problem in aquaculture
propeller_relevance: Category 7 (Organics); Propeller's thinnest named theme; VIMS has no public Propeller partnership

name: Explainable AI for satellite-derived nearshore bathymetry
technology: Explainable AI converting satellite imagery into high-resolution underwater depth maps for coastlines, rivers and lakes
current_maturity: Pre-company; NSF I-Corps customer discovery underway
evidence_signal: NSF I-Corps award 2630206 ($50,000)
why_potentially_interesting: Award abstract states nearly half of US waters remain unmapped to modern standards and that ship- and aircraft-based survey cannot keep pace. Explainability matters because charting is a regulated, liability-bearing domain where black-box depth estimates are unusable
biggest_unknown: Whether satellite-derived bathymetry can reach the accuracy standards hydrographic authorities require, and whether the buyer is government charting (slow) or commercial operators (faster)
propeller_relevance: Category 2 (Industrials/Carbon enabling); ocean data is a stated Propeller interest via Aquatic Labs and Hum.ai

name: AI surrogate for coastal storm surge and water level forecasting
technology: AI surrogate model producing rapid storm surge and water level predictions, replacing slow physics simulations
current_maturity: Pre-company; NSF I-Corps customer discovery underway
evidence_signal: NSF I-Corps award 2633942 ($50,000)
why_potentially_interesting: The abstract names insurance pricing and infrastructure design alongside emergency response - i.e. buyers with real P&Ls, which is the escape route from municipal budgets that sinks most coastal adaptation businesses
biggest_unknown: Forecast skill versus incumbent operational models (NOAA SLOSH, ADCIRC), and whether insurers buy models or buy answers
propeller_relevance: Category 6 (Industrials/adaptation and Carbon/climate risk); matches Propeller's Aug 2026 adaptation thesis

name: Digital workflow for steel infrastructure corrosion inspection, analysis and repair
technology: Digital workflow covering corrosion inspection, analysis and repair for structural steel, targeting the weeks-to-months timelines of conventional plate repair or full asset replacement
current_maturity: Pre-company; NSF I-Corps customer discovery underway
evidence_signal: NSF I-Corps award 2638231 ($50,000)
why_potentially_interesting: Corrosion is explicitly inside Propeller's Industrials theme ('materials') and Allium Engineering proves they buy corrosion. Marine and offshore steel is among the most corrosion-exposed asset classes
biggest_unknown: Whether the marine/offshore segment is the focus at all - the award describes transportation, energy and logistics generally. Ocean-centrality is currently 'adjacent' and would need to be confirmed before this advances
propeller_relevance: Category 5 (Industrials/materials); adjacency to Allium Engineering; MIT has no public Propeller partnership but two portfolio companies trace there

name: BioShield CP: microbial coating system for corrosion protection
technology: Biological (microbial biofilm) coating system for corrosion protection, replacing chemical coatings that carry cost and human/environmental health risks
current_maturity: Pre-company; large multi-year translation award
evidence_signal: NSF Convergence Accelerator award 2452538 ($4,999,999), following Track M award 2344389 ($650,000) - a substantial, staged translation programme
commercialization_signal: NSF Convergence Accelerator is an explicit commercialization-track programme
why_potentially_interesting: The clearest demonstration of this project's core sourcing thesis: a landlocked university with no oceanography department holding a $5M award on the exact problem (biocide-free anticorrosion coatings) that marine assets face most acutely. Would never surface in any ocean-tech search
biggest_unknown: Whether a living microbial coating can survive immersion, biofouling pressure and mechanical wear in seawater specifically - the marine case is much harsher than the terrestrial case the work targets
propeller_relevance: Category 5 (Industrials/materials); Propeller has written about hull coatings; adjacency to Allium and to Fleet Robotics' fouling problem

name: Compact coherent hydrophone arrays for wide-area ocean acoustic monitoring
technology: Passive Ocean Acoustic Waveguide Remote Sensing (POAWRS) using compact coherent hydrophone arrays to monitor wide ocean areas instantaneously from wind farms and other ocean platforms
current_maturity: Pre-company; PFI technology-translation award
evidence_signal: NSF PFI-TT award 2345791 ($550,000) - PFI-TT exists specifically to translate proven research toward commercial application
why_potentially_interesting: Explicitly framed for deployment from offshore wind farms, sitting exactly at the intersection of Propeller's offshore energy and ocean sensing interests. Passive acoustics also serves marine mammal monitoring, which is a regulatory requirement for offshore wind permitting - a mandated buyer
biggest_unknown: Whether wind developers procure monitoring directly or push it to survey contractors, and whether the array cost advantage survives at production volume
propeller_relevance: Category 2/3 (Industrials); adjacency to Indeximate (subsea monitoring) and to the offshore wind biodiversity problems Propeller convened with Orsted at WHOI

name: Sitkana Inc
technology: Modular tidal energy systems for power generation in remote coastal communities currently dependent on diesel generators
current_maturity: Company formed; STTR Phase I awarded
evidence_signal: NSF STTR Phase I award 2507857 ($305,000)
why_potentially_interesting: Targets remote Alaskan coastal communities where the competing cost is diesel generation, not grid power - one of the few settings where marine energy economics can close today. Modularity addresses the installation-cost problem that has killed most tidal projects
biggest_unknown: Whether modular units can be installed and maintained without specialised vessels, which is where marine energy capital costs usually explode
propeller_relevance: Category 3 (Industrials); marine energy is within the Industrials theme, though capital intensity is a real stage-fit concern

name: Reef Arches, LLC
institution_or_company: Reef Arches, LLC (West Palm Beach, FL)
technology: Eco-engineered submerged structures for coastal protection, claimed to reduce wave energy by up to 70% while supporting benthic infauna, seagrass and mangrove habitat
current_maturity: Company formed; SBIR Phase I awarded
evidence_signal: NSF SBIR Phase I award 2528131 ($154,646)
why_potentially_interesting: Specific, testable performance claim (up to 70% wave energy reduction, per the award abstract) rather than a general resilience narrative
biggest_unknown: Whether the 70% figure holds in field conditions and across wave climates, and whether the buyer is a coastal municipality (grant cycles) or a private developer
propeller_relevance: Category 6 (Industrials/adaptation); matches Propeller's coastal adaptation thesis

name: Prime Pacific Enterprises LLC
technology: Autonomous unmanned aerial system for high-precision, repeat monitoring and prediction of coastal erosion
current_maturity: Company formed; SBIR Phase I awarded
evidence_signal: NSF SBIR Phase I award 2528376 ($305,000)
why_potentially_interesting: Hawai'i-based, in a Propeller partner geography (University of Hawai'i), addressing shoreline loss where the asset values at risk are very high
biggest_unknown: Whether autonomous UAS erosion monitoring is a product or a survey service - the services trap is acute here; and how it competes with satellite-derived alternatives
propeller_relevance: Category 6/2 (Industrials/adaptation); University of Hawai'i is a Propeller partner institution

name: Atlantic Fish Co LLC
technology: Bioengineered, commercially viable fish cell lines for cultivated seafood, producing only the required tissue
current_maturity: Company formed; SBIR Phase I awarded
evidence_signal: NSF SBIR Phase I award 2451498 ($305,000)
why_potentially_interesting: Abstract notes 90% of wild fisheries are at or beyond capacity with many premium species lacking viable aquaculture models - a genuine supply constraint. Cell lines are the enabling input layer rather than a consumer product
biggest_unknown: Cultivated meat economics have proven extremely difficult; whether fish cell lines are cheaper to scale than mammalian, and whether the business is licensing cell lines or selling product
propeller_relevance: Category 7 (Organics); Propeller's Organics theme names food and biologic value creation, though no disclosed portfolio company is in cultivated protein

name: Namaka Algae, Inc
technology: Area-efficient cultivation technology that captures and redistributes light into dense microalgae cultures, targeting aquaculture feed
current_maturity: Company formed; SBIR Phase I awarded
evidence_signal: NSF SBIR Phase I award 2451285 ($304,541)
why_potentially_interesting: Attacks the specific physical bottleneck in algae production - light penetration in dense cultures - rather than the general 'algae is promising' thesis, and points at aquafeed, a real existing market
biggest_unknown: Whether the light-distribution advantage translates into a cost per tonne that beats existing feed inputs; algae production has a long history of unmet cost claims
propeller_relevance: Category 7 (Organics); Propeller's Organics theme explicitly names feed; Hawai'i is a Propeller partner geography

name: AI-driven wave prediction for shipping fuel efficiency
technology: Autonomous low-cost ocean sensors feeding real-time wave data into a routing system that helps ships avoid fuel-wasting sea conditions
current_maturity: Pre-company; NSF I-Corps customer discovery underway
evidence_signal: NSF I-Corps award 2533913 ($50,000); Alam's group has a long record in ocean wave hydrodynamics
why_potentially_interesting: The interesting element is the sensor network, not the routing software. Abstract cites over $150B annual shipping fuel spend with more than 20% lost to inefficient routing (attributed to the abstract, not independently verified). Owning proprietary wave data is what would separate this from the crowded weather-routing market
biggest_unknown: Whether proprietary in-situ sensors materially beat existing forecast and satellite products - if not, this is a routing software company in a crowded field
propeller_relevance: Category 8/2 (Industrials); Propeller's Industrials theme names shipping

name: AI and genomics for seafood species identification
technology: Combined AI and genomics enabling rapid, reliable species identification of fish and seafood products in field settings
current_maturity: Pre-company; NSF I-Corps customer discovery underway
evidence_signal: NSF I-Corps award 2348772 ($50,000)
why_potentially_interesting: Seafood traceability and fraud is a large, regulation-driven problem, and Propeller discloses a stealth company in seafood traceability - suggesting the area is live for them
biggest_unknown: Whether field-deployable genomic ID is fast and cheap enough for supply chain use, and who pays: processors, retailers, or regulators. Award is now 19 months old with no public company formation found
propeller_relevance: Category 7 (Organics); a disclosed Propeller stealth company covers seafood traceability, so treat portfolio relationship as unclear

name: Sustainable and resilient enhancement of coastal soils
technology: Soil improvement technique for coastal regions addressing seawater intrusion and soil salinization, where traditional calcium-based stabilisation is ineffective
current_maturity: Pre-company; PFI Research Partnership award
evidence_signal: NSF PFI-RP award 2414953 ($1,000,000) - a research-partnership translation award implying an industry partner
why_potentially_interesting: Salinization-driven degradation of coastal soils is described in the abstract as a hidden hazard to coastal civil infrastructure - an under-addressed failure mode relative to seawalls and surge barriers
biggest_unknown: Whether soil stabilisation is a product, a chemical, or a contracting service - and the qualification timeline for any new geotechnical material is long
propeller_relevance: Category 5/6 (Industrials/materials and adaptation)

name: Statistical physics for maritime diagnostics
technology: Generalizable diagnostic tool tying together disparate, disconnected information sources into a transparent, auditable system, applied to maritime diagnostics
current_maturity: Pre-company; NSF I-Corps customer discovery underway
evidence_signal: NSF I-Corps award 2531191 ($50,000); Michigan hosts one of the few US naval architecture and marine engineering departments
why_potentially_interesting: Michigan's naval architecture department is a rare concentration of maritime engineering talent, and vessel diagnostics is a real operator pain point
biggest_unknown: The award itself describes the technology as platform-independent and applicable to many areas - which is precisely the pattern that indicates the ocean application may be incidental rather than central
propeller_relevance: Category 8 (Industrials); adjacency to Nexxa.ai; ocean-centrality is weak and would need to be established
